claim: Classical empirical methods (Eaton, Miller, Zhang) lose accuracy in heterogeneous offshore carbonates where vuggy porosity and tight intervals disrupt normal compaction trends.
quote: vuggy porosity and tight intervals disrupt normal compaction trends and reduce the reliability of classical empirical approaches, including Eaton, Miller, and Zhang correlations [3,4].

claim: Evaluated on six wells from an Iranian offshore carbonate gas field; classical models after calibration reach R2 0.85-0.90 and RMSE 0.7-1.1 MPa, the hybrid R2 0.94, RMSE 0.45 MPa, MAE 0.32 MPa.
quote: The framework was evaluated on six wells from an Iranian offshore carbonate gas field. After calibration, classical models achieved R2 = 0.85-0.90 with RMSE = 0.7-1.1 MPa, whereas the hybrid model improved cross-well performance to R2 = 0.94, RMSE = 0.45 MPa, and MAE = 0.32 MPa

claim: Depth-wise 95 % confidence bounds are typically within +/- 0.4 MPa.
quote: The UQM reports depth-wise 95% confidence bounds, typically within +/-0.4 MPa, enabling risk-aware mud-weight planning.

claim: Eaton sonic form P_p = sigma_v - (sigma_v - P_n)(delta t_n/delta t)^x with x typically 3.0.
quote: = empirically determined exponent (typically 3.0 for sonic logs)

claim: MDT/XPT pressure points are the ground truth for calibration; coverage is about 2850-3440 m TVD with 26-33 valid points per well, and one well is blind.
quote: For one well (B-08), complete MDT/XPT pressure data were not available due to operational limitations. This well was therefore excluded from calibration and used as a blind prediction case

claim: Adaptive calibration cut Well C RMSE from 1.02 to 0.56 MPa, with the largest gains in stylolitic and vuggy intervals.
quote: The non-adaptive model resulted in an RMSE of 1.02 MPa, while the ACL reduced it to 0.56 MPa, showing a 45% improvement.

claim: Performance depends on log quality (washouts, missing segments); future work is pre-drill prediction from seismic inversion and cross-field validation.
quote: In regions with poor log quality, uncertainties can be significant, stemming from issues like severe borehole washouts, missing data segments or formation damage that hinders signal reliability.
